proposition.claim:
For an open set \(Z\subset\mathbb R^4\), the source defines \[V_d(Z)=\operatorname{vol}\{z\in Z:\operatorname{dist}(z,\partial Z)<d\},\qquad
 q=\liminf_{d\downarrow0}\frac{\log V_d(Z)}{\log d}.\] Equation (2.2), p. 7, calls this number the order of volume decay. It is a logarithmic exponent and does not assert \(V_d=O(d^q)\). The inner upper Minkowski dimension is \(4-q\). The subleading capacity term is \(e_k(Z)=c_k(Z)-2\sqrt{k\operatorname{vol}Z}\). A four-dimensional ball of capacity \(a\) has radius \(\sqrt{a/\pi}\) and volume \(a^2/2\). The ball and disjoint-union capacity formulas used below are stated in Section 2.2 and used in (4.4)–(4.6), pp. 16–17.

If a relatively compact open Z has volume-decay order q, there is C>0 depending only on Z such that e_k(Z)>-C k^((2-q)/4) for all k.

For an open set \(Z\subset\mathbb R^4\), the source defines \[V_d(Z)=\operatorname{vol}\{z\in Z:\operatorname{dist}(z,\partial Z)<d\},\qquad
 q=\liminf_{d\downarrow0}\frac{\log V_d(Z)}{\log d}.\] Equation (2.2), p. 7, calls this number the order of volume decay. It is a logarithmic exponent and does not assert \(V_d=O(d^q)\). The inner upper Minkowski dimension is \(4-q\). The subleading capacity term is \(e_k(Z)=c_k(Z)-2\sqrt{k\operatorname{vol}Z}\). A four-dimensional ball of capacity \(a\) has radius \(\sqrt{a/\pi}\) and volume \(a^2/2\). The ball and disjoint-union capacity formulas used below are stated in Section 2.2 and used in (4.4)–(4.6), pp. 16–17.

The displayed composition is a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism used in the bounded symplectic realization.

For an open set \(Z\subset\mathbb R^4\), the source defines \[V_d(Z)=\operatorname{vol}\{z\in Z:\operatorname{dist}(z,\partial Z)<d\},\qquad
 q=\liminf_{d\downarrow0}\frac{\log V_d(Z)}{\log d}.\] Equation (2.2), p. 7, calls this number the order of volume decay. It is a logarithmic exponent and does not assert \(V_d=O(d^q)\). The inner upper Minkowski dimension is \(4-q\). The subleading capacity term is \(e_k(Z)=c_k(Z)-2\sqrt{k\operatorname{vol}Z}\). A four-dimensional ball of capacity \(a\) has radius \(\sqrt{a/\pi}\) and volume \(a^2/2\). The ball and disjoint-union capacity formulas used below are stated in Section 2.2 and used in (4.4)–(4.6), pp. 16–17.

The convex domain is the radius-d tube around its inner erosion, giving V_d=N_d(Z(d))-N_0(Z(d)).
